`send_receipt()` in `services/notifier/notifier/email.py` now logs when the send fails. I didn't run it or any tests.

It wraps the `send(...)` call in a `try/except Exception`. On failure it calls `log.exception("receipt send failed", extra={"invoice_id": invoice_id})` and then re-raises, so callers still see the error.

- **Logger:** it uses the stdlib `logging` logger, as the notifier logging convention requires, and passes context through `extra=`.
- **No PII:** the log has only the invoice id. `to_addr` is left out because of the no-customer-PII-in-logs rule. `log.exception` also writes the traceback. If the provider's exception message includes the recipient address, it would end up in the logs. I haven't checked what `provider.send` raises.
- **Customer id:** `send_receipt()` doesn't receive one, so I logged `invoice_id` instead. If you want the customer id in the log, it would need to be passed in.
